newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah ends higher in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah ends higher in slow late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah ended up against the dollar in dull trade on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said month-end factors appeared to have kept the rupiah firm amid ample liquidity supply.

One U.S. bank dealer said the underlying tone was not as bullish as on Tuesday when comments by Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad about the central bank's band widening being positive for debt payments triggered a rise in the rupiah.
"I still expect some dollar strengthening on Thursday. But I think the upside is limited," the dealer said.
One-month swap was at 14.0/15.0, two at 30.0/31.1, three at 43.50/44.25 and six at 87.50/88.25 points.
The central bank kept its intervention rate unchanged at 2,342/2,534 and the conversion rate at 2,342/2,390.
The U.S. bank dealer said the unchanged fixing also seemed to cause some dollar selling late in the afternoon. But others said they anticipated a higher fixing on Thursday.

A local bank dealer said the dollar could also strengthen on Thursday because any deals would mature only in December because of the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States,, which could create fresh buying interest.
Spot rupiah closed at 2,343.25/43.50 against an opening of 2,2,344.0/45.0. Today ended at 2,343.75/44.00. There was no trading in value tomorrow because of the Thanksgiving holiday.
Dealers said longer-term swap rates were driven up slightly by rises in short-dated swaps due to month-end factors.
Overnight swap was at 0.6/0.7 and spot/next at 1.35/1.45.
